security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel context-switches a thread with sivt.EHV set without sanitizing or saving/restoring the EHV bit, or the kernel itself runs with EHV enabled and synchronous exceptions are hardware-vectored through the ivt-based offset instead of the stvec handler, bypassing the kernel's trap entry code that expects a unified synchronous exception path.
security_spec.summary: Ssehv introduces supervisor-level synchronous exception hardware vectoring via sivt.EHV; FreeBSD's trap entry at stvec must ensure EHV is never enabled in kernel mode or properly save/restore it per-thread to prevent trap-routing bypass.

findings.finding: Boot path initializes stvec to cpu_exception_handler in Direct mode (address written without mode bits), which neutralizes any EHV vectoring effect. However, sivt (CSR 0x107) is never cleared — the CSR retains whatever value firmware left. This is a defense-in-depth gap but not exploitable because stvec Direct mode (mode=00) means EHV has no effect per ACLIC spec: synchronous exceptions always go to stvec.BASE regardless of EHV setting.
findings.snippet:
la	t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw	stvec, t0

li	t0, 0
csrw	sscratch, t0

spec_citations.excerpt:
mode  PC on Synchronous Exception
00       OBASE              # Direct mode
01       OBASE              # Vectored mode
11       OBASE+4*exccode    # Interrupt vector table mode
10       Reserved

When {xivt}.{EHV} is set, the synchronous exceptions trap to [these] entry point[s]
As this specification aims for single-hart systems, no support for the H extension is foreseen.

findings.finding: Same pattern as primary boot: stvec set to Direct mode, neutralizing any inherited sivt.EHV. No sivt sanitization but no exploitability.
findings.snippet:
la	t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw	stvec, t0

li	t0, 0
csrw	sscratch, t0

findings.finding: Trap entry uses sscratch-based user/supervisor dispatch. All synchronous exceptions arrive via stvec Direct mode (single entry point). No risk of bypass because stvec is never set to Vectored mode (mode=01) or Interrupt Vector Table mode (mode=11), so EHV has no effect even if set in sivt.
findings.snippet:
csrrw	sp, sscratch, sp
beqz	sp, 1f
j	cpu_exception_handler_user
1:
csrrw	sp, sscratch, sp
j	cpu_exception_handler_supervisor

findings.finding: No CSR_SIVT (0x107) or CSR_SEIVT (0x108) numeric definitions exist. No DECLARE_CSR(sivt, ...) macro. This is expected — these CSRs belong to the ACLIC microcontroller extension (Ssivt/Ssehv), not the base privileged ISA, and are not needed for a general-purpose OS kernel.
findings.snippet: (CSR definitions from 0x001 to 0x7xx — sivt 0x107 absent, seivt 0x108 absent)

spec_citations.excerpt:
0x107   sivt         S-mode Interrupt-handler vector table base address
0x108   seivt        S-mode External Interrupt-handler vector table base address

findings.finding: Context switch saves/restores only GPRs and FPU state. No sivt save/restore — but sivt is not used by the kernel (stvec Direct mode), so no state is lost and no security property is violated. The CSR is effectively dead state.
findings.snippet: (cpu_throw and cpu_switch save/restore ra, sp, s0-s11, FPU — no CSR state beyond what's in trapframe)

findings.finding: trapframe lacks sivt field — consistent with the kernel not using the Ssivt extension. No violation because the kernel never programs sivt.

VMM hypervisor world-switch saves/restores hstatus, sstatus, scounteren, sscratch, stvec, sepc — all standard hypervisor CSRs. sivt is not saved/restored, but this is consistent: the ACLIC spec explicitly excludes H-extension support, so sivt is not relevant in a virtualized context.
findings.snippet:
csrrw	t0, sstatus, t0
csrrw	t1, hstatus, t1
csrrw	t2, scounteren, t2
csrrw	t3, sscratch, a0
csrrw	t4, stvec, t4
csrw	sepc, t5

spec_citations.excerpt: As this specification aims for single-hart systems, no support for the H extension is foreseen.

findings.finding: Guest virtual supervisor CSR structure (hypcsr) lists all standard VS-level CSRs: vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, vsatp, scounteren, senvcfg. No vsivt field — correct, because ACLIC extensions are explicitly not designed for H-extension systems.

spec_citations.excerpt: As this specification aims for single-hart systems, no support for the H extension is foreseen.
